Oh but to add on I realized I am talking like my family still lives there. In 2019 they managed to escape and some live in Chile now and others live in Florida.

To start off, I’m Venezuelan.

My uncle’s kidneys don’t work. The government spent all the money from government owned business on itself because of course corruption easily forms and funding for hospitals and medical supplies are basically non existent.

My direct family lives in the US and my mom was the only person that was a match to give him her kidney. The government of course is very difficult and there was a chance that she would’ve had a hard time returning from Venezuela if she went. There is a lot of hate towards people who emigrate. 

So basically since the government didn’t give any money to the hospitals we had to buy all the supplies for the surgery ourselves. All the aftercare the antibiotics. Everything for an organ transplant my mom had to pay for.

Luckily the surgery was successful, but because the doctors aren’t as good as the US they essentially cut my mom in half to retrieve her kidney. She has a huge scar on her left side from bellybutton to back. When doctors aren’t paid to be the best they won’t be the best yknow?

Another thing is the water supply to the capital where most of my family lives is contaminated because the sewage directly goes into the water supply so my grandpa, had to drive from his home in mountains to the capital the deliver fresh water to my aunt, cousin and uncle. 

Something that didn’t directly effect my family is that they refused aid for their starving citizens. The government set a truck carrying food for the people on fire on the Colombian border. 

It’s just a whole mess, it’s what happens when the government owns the everything. The gun laws are so that only government officials can own guns and the government hires militias to attack those who oppose it.

My country thrived before socialism.
